prompt.context: Your client is a major distilled spirits manufacturer with a number of major brands.
prompt.question: What should the focus of their advertising budget be? What sized advertising budget would be needed to follow through on your strategy?

clarifying_info.q: What market segment is the client competing in?
clarifying_info.a: They are competing in the premium scotch segment (think Johnnie Walker Black).

clarifying_info.q: Who are the competitors and what is our market share?
clarifying_info.a: The client is the #3 brand with just under 20% share. The #1 brand has just over 20% share and the #2 brand is just below the #1 brand. There is also a distant #4 brand.

clarifying_info.q: How significant is advertising as a cost?
clarifying_info.a: Advertising is a significant portion of the cost structure of premium scotch brands — over 25% of sales.

clarifying_info.q: What did competitors spend on advertising last year and what happened to their share?
clarifying_info.a: The #1 player spent heavily on advertising and increased share. The #2 player spent nothing and lost share. The client spent a little more than nothing and increased share slightly. The #4 brand spent nothing on advertising.

framework: Customers: Identify target segment, analyze demographics, determine effective advertising media mix, and define brand qualities to stress
Competitors: Assess competitive positioning and market share, understand link between ad spend and share movement, identify minimum scale required to advertise profitably
Company (budget): Evaluate three budget-setting alternatives — match #1 competitor, incremental increase over prior year, or bottom-up cost build of the proposed strategy

questions.prompt: What should be the focus of the advertising strategy?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply a 3 C's lens. On Customers: identify the premium scotch segment and its target demo (affluent males 30+), map which media channels reach them (print magazines, billboards, golf sponsorships), and determine what brand qualities to emphasize (status, taste, distinction). On Competitors: note the positive correlation between ad spend and share growth observed across the competitive set, and flag the minimum-scale dynamic — higher volume yields more resources for advertising, creating a reinforcing advantage for the leader.

questions.prompt: What sized advertising budget would be needed?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose three alternative budget approaches: (1) Match the #1 competitor's spend to keep pace with the market leader; (2) Incrementally increase versus the client's prior-year spend as a lower-risk step up; (3) Build a bottom-up cost model of the specific ads, sponsorships, and media placements identified in the strategy and quantify the actual dollar requirement. A strong answer explains the tradeoffs — option 1 is competitive but may be unaffordable; option 3 is the most analytically rigorous but requires more data.

brainstorming.prompt: What media channels and campaign elements should the client use to reach affluent males 30+ for a premium scotch brand?

categories.name: Print
ideas: Selected luxury and lifestyle magazines (e.g., Forbes, Golf Digest, Robb Report)
Full-page spread ads emphasizing brand heritage and quality

categories.name: Sponsorship
ideas: Golf tournament sponsorships (e.g., PGA Tour events)
Sponsorship of polo, sailing, or other premium-perceived sports
Hospitality suites at major sporting events

categories.name: Events & Experiential
ideas: Whiskey tasting events at upscale venues
Brand ambassador programs at premium bars and restaurants

categories.name: Outdoor
ideas: Premium billboard placements in affluent urban neighborhoods and airports

recommendation: Focus advertising on the premium scotch segment targeting affluent males 30+ through a curated media mix of luxury print, golf sponsorships, and select upscale events
Set the advertising budget using a bottom-up strategy cost build as the primary approach, benchmarked against the #1 competitor's spend to ensure competitive parity
risks: If budget falls short of the minimum viable scale, advertising spend may be insufficient to drive meaningful share gains
The positive correlation between ad spend and share is empirical from one year of data and may not hold in all competitive environments
Matching the #1 competitor may strain resources if the client lacks the volume base to sustain that level of spend profitably
next_steps: Conduct market research to confirm target segment demographics and most effective media channels
Quantify the cost of the proposed media plan (number of ads, sponsorships, placements) to build the bottom-up budget
Model the revenue impact of share gains at various spending levels to determine the ROI-maximizing budget level
